en: Old Tokaido and the Checkpoint: Walk the Road, Read the System
zh: 旧东海道与箱根关所：走一段路，读一种制度
ja: 旧東海道と箱根関所：道を歩き、制度を読む

p.src: Leave Moto-Hakone's cedar avenue and the old road changes from a stroll into a search for secure footing. Stones vary in size; gaps, shallow drains, and repaired patches interrupt the surface. After rain, shorten each step. Hakone Town identifies this as part of the Edo-period Tokaido known as Hakone Hachiri. What can be walked today combines surviving paving and cedar-lined sections with later conservation and maintenance. The four guides check grip, daylight, knees, and ankles before deciding whether to continue to Amasake Chaya or return to a bus stop. There is no need to chase mileage: walk one mountain section carefully and see how the paved road crosses the slope.

caption.zh: 雨后的旧街道石板路高低不平。先看石缝、排水和鞋底抓地，再决定是否继续到甘酒茶屋。
caption.ja: 雨上がりの旧街道石畳は凹凸が大きい。石の隙間、排水、靴底のグリップを見てから、甘酒茶屋まで進むか決める。
caption.en: The old-road paving remains uneven after rain. Read gaps, drainage, and shoe grip before deciding whether to continue to Amasake Chaya.

p.src: The map keeps two routes with practical finishing points. If uneven paving is unsuitable, visit the checkpoint, walk the cedar avenue, allow 60 to 90 minutes, then leave by bus from the lakeshore. For one coherent old-road section, follow the checkpoint, cedar avenue, Old Road Entrance, stone paving, and Amasake Chaya in that order. The tourism association gives about 2 hours 30 minutes for its guided route; the checkpoint visit, tea-house break, and bus wait come in addition. Amasake Chaya is on route K, but departure and destination require a same-day check. The Hatajuku-Yamane section is currently scheduled to remain closed through 15 January 2027 and is left out of this chapter's walking route.

caption.zh: 从箱根关所选择杉木林荫道短线，或沿一段石板路走到甘酒茶屋；畑宿山根段标出当前施工封闭。位置不按比例，时间不是班次。
caption.ja: 箱根関所から杉並木の短い歩き方、または石畳を甘酒茶屋まで歩く方法を選ぶ。畑宿山根区間は現在の工事通行止めを表示。位置は縮尺外で、時間は時刻表ではない。
caption.en: Choose the short checkpoint-and-cedars visit or one stone section ending at Amasake Chaya. The current Hatajuku-Yamane works are marked; positions are not to scale and times are not a timetable.

p.src: Hakone Town says that paving walked by Edo-period travellers and cedar-lined sections survive; it does not say that the entire route has never been altered. A historic road still meets rain, roots, and foot traffic, so drainage, repaving, temporary closures, and conservation are part of keeping it open. Read stone size, road edges, and the way water is carried off instead of guessing the age of one block. Without on-site interpretation, do not assign a date or story to an individual stone. The old road is both a historic site and a working mountain path exposed to rain and roots.

p.src: Hakone Town announced that the old-road section between Hatajuku and Yamane will close for construction from 17 August 2026 to a planned 15 January 2027. The milestone and paving in that section cannot be visited, and the notice directs a detour to Prefectural Road 732. This guide does not turn that vehicle-road detour into a leisure walk: finish at Amasake Chaya and take the bus. On any open section, wear shoes with grip, keep both hands free, and leave wheeled luggage elsewhere. Standing water, ice, fallen trees, barriers, or fading light are reasons to return to the nearest safe exit and bus stop.

p.src: At Hakone Checkpoint, stand outside the Edo-side gate before turning to figures and exhibits. Shore, palisade, and hillside narrow the road to a single passage, and the reason for this location becomes clear from the gate. The official history places the checkpoint on this site around 1619, but today's buildings are not original fabric. The reconstruction drew on an 1865 repair-completion record, excavated remains, and traditional building methods, with the present works completed in 2007. It is a reconstruction grounded in documents and archaeology, not a group of four-hundred-year-old buildings left intact.

caption.zh: 从江户口御门看木栅、复原建筑与山坡远见番所；现建筑依据文书和发掘成果复原。
caption.ja: 江戸口御門から木柵、復元建物、斜面の遠見番所を見る。現建物は文書と発掘成果に基づく復元である。
caption.en: Read the Edo-side gate, palisade, reconstructed buildings, and hillside lookout together. The buildings are evidence-based reconstructions.

p.src: 'Incoming guns and outgoing women' summarises shogunal concern with weapons and movement; it was not one checklist used at every checkpoint. Hakone's 1711 rules required travellers to uncover their faces, conveyances to be opened, women leaving Edo to match their documents, and injured, dead, or suspicious people to carry papers. Pre-notified court or daimyo parties normally passed without inspection, except when someone appeared suspicious. Hakone Town adds that this checkpoint did not inspect weapons entering Edo and was strict with outgoing women. What survives is evidence of a routine system governing identity, papers, exceptions, and unequal freedom to travel.

p.src: The official standard visit is about 45 minutes. Enter through the Edo-side gate, read the posted rules, then move through reconstructed spaces such as the senior guard station and its rest room before the documentary displays. The hillside lookout adds a climb and return; omit it if the footing or weather is unsuitable. Finish in the museum by connecting the 1865 record, excavation, and reconstruction process. As checked on 20 August 2026, official hours are 09:00-17:00 from March through November and 09:00-16:30 from December through February, with last entry 30 minutes before closing; recheck before departure. The site is about five minutes on foot from Hakone-machi port.

p.src: At Amasake Chaya, treat it first as a rest on the mountain road, not a historical set. The current proprietor is the thirteenth generation, and the clearest living connection with the old road is the amazake still served here. It is made only from rice koji and rice, with no added sugar or alcohol. Chikara-mochi is charcoal-grilled and comes in soy-and-nori isobe, green-soybean uguisu, and limited black sesame. The four guides order one cup each and share a plate of two mochi, enough for a proper pause without mistaking the tea house for lunch. After the stone-paved climb, the reason for a tea house here is easy to understand.

caption.zh: 米曲甘酒与一盘力饼正好构成旧路上的短休息。这里的甘酒不加糖，也不含酒精；返程班次仍要先查。
caption.ja: 米麹の甘酒と力餅一皿で、旧街道の短い休憩にする。ここの甘酒は砂糖不使用、ノンアルコール。帰りの便は先に確かめる。
caption.en: Rice-koji amazake and one plate of chikara-mochi make a route-sized rest. This shop's drink has no added sugar or alcohol; check the onward bus first.

p.src: As checked on 20 August 2026, the shop lists 07:00-17:30 hours, a 17:00 last order, and no scheduled closing day; the Amasake Chaya bus stop is beside it. Hakone-Yumoto's current transport page describes route K as the old-road line via Hatajuku and Amasake Chaya, but not every departure runs towards your next stop. On arrival, check the next time, direction, and destination before deciding whether there is room for amazake, mochi, or both. This shop explicitly describes its amazake as non-alcoholic; confirm ingredients again when ordering a drink with the same name elsewhere.

p.src: With a full morning, give the checkpoint about 45 minutes, walk the cedar avenue, then continue to Amasake Chaya only if the surface, weather, and your legs are suitable. End the walk at the tea house and use route K towards the lodging or transfer point. When continuing after lunch from the Lake Ashi route in Chapter 5, keep that day to the checkpoint and cedars, leaving the stone section for the next morning. Do not add the lower Hatajuku extension during the current works. Before stepping onto the first stone, write down the lodging's latest check-in and dinner time. Do not delay either one merely to add another stretch of paving.
